stem:
Aarav chews plain boiled rice for about one minute. It begins to taste sweet. He places iodine on unchewed boiled rice and on the chewed rice. He also has egg white as a protein food that is not starch.

Answer both parts.

options.text: Saliva breaks starch in the rice into sugar, so the chewed rice gives a weaker blue-black iodine colour than the unchewed rice.
Unchewed boiled rice also gives little or no blue-black colour with iodine.
Saliva changes the protein in egg white into sugar.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: The sweet taste and the weaker iodine colour show that some starch has been broken into sugar by saliva; saliva does not turn egg-white protein into sugar.

teacher.key_rationale: Saliva breaks starch into sugar. Unchewed rice still has starch for a strong iodine test; saliva does not act on egg-white protein that way.
